newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 17.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Thursday:
- Apple Computer Inc reported a $25 million profit for its fiscal fourth quarter, surprising the stock market, which had expected worse.
- Institutional investors gather at the annual meeting of Archer Daniels Midland Co in the hopes of putting an independent director on the company's board.
- U.S. consumer prices rose slightly in September, partly due to seasonal quirks and the return of a tax on airline tickets.
- Advertising campaigns are encouraging Germans to buy stock in the country's telephone company Deutsche Telekom as part of a government effort to create a stock culture.
- General Motors Corp Chairman John Smith met with Basil Hargrove of the Canadian Automobile Workers union to set a Monday deadline to reach a comprehensive labor deal and end a massive strike.
- Ford Motor Co reported $686 million or $0.56 per share for the third quarter.
- Compaq Computer Corp reported gains in revenues, earnings and profit for the quarter.
- AT&T Corp's board of directors discussed a candidate for the company's presidency. The company is to announce third-quarter earnings on Thursday and a new president next week.
- Sears, Roebuck and Co's third-quarter earnings rose 22 percenty due to sales of apparel, hardware and furniture.
- Time Warner Inc and U S West Media Group discussed a possible settlement over the ownership of Time Warner Entertainment.
- Pharmaceutical companies see their stocks rise in price for a third year in a row as they launch new products.
- The Dow Jones Industrial average surpassed Monday's record close, ending at 6,020.81. U.S. Treasury bond prices closed lower as a result of inflation fears.
- Mexico's peso fell to its lowest level this year as investors worry about the government's privatisation programme.
